Timeline::months_between¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Timeline::months_between(const Timeline& other) const

Count Complete Calendar-Month Movements¶

months_between() answers how many whole calendar-month movements fit between two scalar instants. Read a.months_between(b) as “the signed number of complete months from a to b.” It returns a native integer, not a one-element Series, and is intended for scalar control flow and interval classification.

This is calendar arithmetic in the shared timezone. It is not elapsed duration divided by an average month length; months have no fixed nanosecond size. The method first estimates the calendar-month separation, moves the earlier instant by that many months using the same clamping rule as add_months(), and counts the final month only if that anniversary has been reached.

Both operands must be scalar, defined instants with identical tz() names. The result is antisymmetric: reversing the operands reverses the sign without changing the magnitude.

Example: End-Of-Month Clamping Defines The Anniversary¶

const auto start = pluss::timeline::make("2023-01-31T10:00:00Z");
const auto anniversary = pluss::timeline::make("2023-02-28T10:00:00Z");
const auto one_second_early =
    pluss::timeline::make("2023-02-28T09:59:59Z");

std::cout << "complete=" << start.months_between(anniversary) << '\n'
          << "incomplete=" << start.months_between(one_second_early) << '\n';

Output¶

complete=1
incomplete=0

Adding one month to 31 January clamps to the last valid day of February while preserving 10:00. Consequently, 28 February at 10:00 completes one month; 09:59:59 does not. This rule also handles 29, 30, and 31-day month boundaries without introducing an arbitrary average month.

Example: Direction Is Encoded In The Sign¶

const auto january = pluss::timeline::make("2023-01-31T10:00:00Z");
const auto february = pluss::timeline::make("2023-02-28T10:00:00Z");

std::cout << january.months_between(february) << '\n'
          << february.months_between(january) << '\n';

Output¶

1
-1

Intervals shorter than one complete month return zero in either direction. There is no negative zero.

Example: Calendar Zones Must Match¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-01-01T00:00:00Z");
const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");

try {
  (void)utc.months_between(local);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected

The two values represent the same instant, but their displayed calendars use different zones. A calendar-month answer would therefore have no single civil frame of reference. Convert one operand explicitly before calling.

Failures And Cost¶

Vectors, matrices, NaT, or mismatched timezone names throw before a result is returned. The method performs constant work and allocates only the temporary scalar anniversary needed to apply calendar clamping. For elementwise or broadcasted distances, use span() with TimelineSpanUnit::Months; that method returns a shape-preserving Series and offers boundary, completion, anchor, and sign policies.

See Also¶

  • add_months: construct a calendar-month anniversary.

  • years_between: count complete calendar years.

  • span: calculate configurable elementwise spans.
